newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico confiscates property of top drug traffickers.
newsitem.headline: Mexico confiscates property of top drug traffickers.

text.p: Mexico's Attorney General's Office said on Thursday it had confiscated four real estate properties owned by the Arellano Felix brothers who allegedly control one of Mexico's largest drug cartels.

"Today in the (northern border) city of Tijuana, four residential properties of the Arellano Felix brothers were confiscated, in which more than 76 kilograms (167 pounds) of cocaine and five kilograms (11 pounds) of marijuana were decomissioned," authorities said in a news release.

Authorities said three of the Arellando Felix brothers - Ramon, Francisco Javier and Benjamin - run the Tijuana or Frontera (Border) cartel. The government has placed a $1 million bounty on each of their heads.
U.S. authorities have called the Tijuana cartel among the most violent criminal organisations in Mexico.
